newsitem.title: USA: Ontario Hydro restarts fifth Pickering nuke unit.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro restarts fifth Pickering nuke unit.

text.p: Ontario Hydro restarted a fifth unit at its Pickering generating complex and has operated it at low level power, the company said Tuesday.
"It is back at minimal power," said utility spokesman Ted Gruetzner, adding the number seven unit was expected to resume full output "over the next few days."
Also producing electricity were two units in the "B" half of the complex and two at the "A" side, Gruetzner noted.
All eight units at the Pickering facility, each with a capacity of 540 megawatts (MW), were shut April 20 after a problem with backup valve on an emergency cooling system.
The Pickering "A" 3 unit was still scheduled to return to service on October 31, Gruetzner said.
But remaining units--"A" 4 and "B" 8--will not resume operation until March 1997, he said.
"They are not planned to be in service until the new year," he said.
Ontario Hydro has an overall in-service generation capacity of just over 29,000 MW.
